draft.title: The spheres and biomes
card: A biome depends on four linked parts of Earth. Each is called a sphere.
the atmosphere is the air, which brings sunlight, heat and rain. The hydrosphere is the water, such as rivers, lakes, oceans and groundwater.
the lithosphere is the rock and soil, which hold nutrients. The biosphere is all living things, such as plants and animals.

The spheres work together, so a change to one can change the others. Clearing forest removes plants from the biosphere. The soil can then wash away and the local water supply can change. Mining digs into the lithosphere and can also affect water and living things.
draft.remember: The spheres are linked, so a human change to one can change the whole biome.

a.q: Which sphere is made up of rock and soil?
opts: The lithosphere
The atmosphere
The hydrosphere
The biosphere
a.why: The lithosphere is the rock and soil. The biosphere is tempting because plants grow in soil, but the biosphere is the living things, not the soil itself.
a.clue: Think about which sphere holds nutrients for plants.

b.q: A company clears a hillside forest in Tasmania for farmland. Soon after, heavy rain washes soil into a nearby river. Which statement best explains this?
opts: Clearing plants changed the biosphere and exposed the soil
Clearing plants changed the biosphere and left the river alone
The rain changed the lithosphere, which then removed plants
The river changed the atmosphere, which then removed plants
b.why: The spheres are linked. Clearing plants changed the biosphere, and this left the soil in the lithosphere open to wash into the hydrosphere. The option saying the river was left alone is tempting, but a change to one sphere can affect the others.
b.clue: Follow the change from plants to soil to water.
